title: What If an Astronaut Dropped a Tool Bag? It Orbited Earth for 8 Months

scenes.text: What if an astronaut let go of a tool bag on a spacewalk? In 2008, one did.
On November 18th, a grease gun leaked inside the bag. During the cleanup, the bag floated off.
It was the size of a backpack, held two grease guns and a scraper, and cost 100,000 dollars.
It didn't fall. It became a satellite, circling Earth a few minutes ahead of the station.
Within days, backyard skywatchers found it with ordinary binoculars, a faint dot crossing the stars.
It circled for more than eight months before burning up in August 2009. In 2023, astronauts lost another one.

description:
What if an astronaut let go of a tool bag on a spacewalk? On 18 November 2008, during shuttle mission STS-126 at the International Space Station, a backpack-sized bag worth about 100,000 dollars drifted away while a leaking grease gun was being cleaned up.
The bag went into its own orbit a few minutes ahead of the station and, at about magnitude 6.4, was just too faint for the naked eye but visible in binoculars. It stayed up for more than eight months and burned up on 3 August 2009; Guinness lists it as the largest object lost on a spacewalk. On 1 November 2023 another bag was lost the same way and could also be seen with binoculars.
